title: Gado-Gado
subtitle: Indonesian vegetable salad with peanut sauce
excerpt: Gado-gado is an Indonesian salad of cooked and raw vegetables, hard-boiled eggs, and tofu, covered in a warm peanut sauce. It is one of Indonesia's national dishes and is as satisfying as any cooked meal. The peanut sauce is the centrepiece -- rich, sweet, and tangy.
sourceNotes: Gado-gado (meaning mix-mix) is one of Indonesia's most celebrated national dishes. It originated in the Betawi culture of Jakarta. The dish is a complete meal in itself -- protein from eggs, carbohydrate from potato, and a variety of vegetables. The peanut sauce is thicker and richer than the Thai version served with satay.

content.text: Gado-gado is a dish where the peanut sauce does the heavy lifting. The vegetables can vary -- use whatever is to hand. The key is to blanch each one separately so they keep their colour and texture. The sauce goes on warm, not hot, and should be thick enough to cling to the vegetables.

items.prepNote: hard-boiled -- 10 minutes, then peeled and halved
boiled whole until tender, then sliced
blanched for 3 minutes in salted boiling water
cut into batons and blanched for 2 minutes
use 5 tbsp peanut butter -- for the sauce
use 100ml coconut milk -- for the peanut sauce
juice of half a lime -- for the sauce

content.text: Prepare all the vegetables: boil the potatoes until just tender. Blanch the beans, carrot, and cabbage separately in salted boiling water. Drain each and set aside. Hard-boil the eggs for 10 minutes.

Make the peanut sauce: whisk the peanut butter with coconut milk, soy sauce, lime juice, brown sugar, chilli flakes, and salt in a small saucepan over low heat. Stir until smooth. Add a little warm water to loosen if needed.
Arrange the vegetables and halved eggs on a large plate or individual plates.
Pour the warm peanut sauce generously over the vegetables.
Serve with prawn crackers on the side if available.

items.symptom: Peanut sauce splits and looks oily
items.fix: Warm the peanut sauce over the lowest heat possible. If it splits, add a splash of warm water and stir gently in one direction until it comes back together. Never let it boil.

content.text: Gado-gado is one of Indonesia's national dishes. It is eaten across the country in different forms -- some versions are more salad-like, others are closer to a composed platter. The peanut sauce in Indonesia is usually thicker than the Thai satay sauce. The dish is a meal in itself -- filling, nutritious, and very satisfying.
